reason: The circuit captures the product pair ranked by revenue and the revenue-share question, but marks the opening command ‘Give me’ as interrogative.
‘Says’ takes ‘the girl wants to switch to ginger’ as its complement. The source makes the wanting an independent clause and reports ‘it suits her’ as what she says.
The circuit marks the suggestion as declarative and treats “clipped” as a modifier of the grid lines. It is the complement of causative “have” and expresses what should happen to the lines.
The circuit treats ‘Start’ as a nonfinite predicate. Start is the named recipient of the two dimensions, and the coordination incorrectly joins ‘180’ with ‘height’.
The imperative routes ‘that arrow’ around Verify and preserves both ‘now’ and ‘instead’.
The circuit preserves the “can you” question and identifies a bird as what the addressee is asked to add.
It places the bench near the tent and links both 'on top of that' and 'on the bench' to putting the lantern.

It locates the bench near the tent and attaches the second instruction's placement phrases to 'put'.
The command moves the woman with the yellow hat one spot to the right. The hat identifies the woman, and the direction and distance modify the move.
The circuit preserves the rightward direction and one-spot distance, but attaches “with the yellow hat” to the move. The phrase identifies the woman.
The interrogative makes the sun the subject of ‘shine’ and ‘what’ the complement of ‘on’.
The sun is correctly the subject of “shine,” but “on” is assigned a result role. The question asks for the object of the stranded preposition “on.”
The circuit makes ‘striped’ a declarative predicate with ‘spread’ as its subject. The source commands ‘spread’ and uses ‘striped’ to modify ‘pattern’.
The imperative makes the ear the object of ‘change’ and preserves ‘large’, ‘big’, and ‘pale’ as properties of that ear.
The circuit captures the background statement and the transparency command, but attaches ‘group’ to ‘transparent’. The object of ‘set’ is the Harbour group.
The circuit preserves the polite ‘Could you’ request to create an orange hexagon, links Membrane as its label, and captures the separate thanks.
The need, making, and appreciation clauses have their participants, but ‘labelled’ is marked declarative instead of forming a reduced passive modifier of ‘diamond.’
The speaker needs the addressee to make a yellow diamond bearing the label ‘Q1 plan,’ and then expresses appreciation.

The circuit treats ‘glow’ as a noun in the object of ‘make,’ losing the predicate that applies to all boxes.

Door and Chair are coordinated objects of ‘set,’ and the ‘so’ clause specifies that their right edges are to be level.

The with relation links the quoted sentence to Team update itself, assigning it the wrong attachment for the replacement.

The circuit names the object ‘Publish 300 px’ and treats the left as the movement source. The object is ‘Publish,’ and 300 px is the requested offset from the left.
The sequence keeps a title line at the top of the approval-flow diagram, then places a caption under the figure with enough space between the parts.
The circuit invents a separate imperative ‘space’ from the noun phrase ‘enough space’ and splits the object ‘title line’ into an object and a predicate complement.
The bird is the object of turning, but the house location attaches to the action and the big brown owl is encoded as a destination instead of the resulting form.
The circuit captures the owl’s size and color, but encodes the owl as an in location and attaches the house to the action rather than the bird.
The circuit places the bird in the owl through an in relation. The source asks for the bird to become the owl.
